l: angel of the assembly in Laodicea, Revelation
s: The angel of the assembly in Laodicea is the addressee of the third message in this unit, which is written to him. The speaker's words to the assembly come through this angel.

The assembly in Laodicea is lukewarm, neither cold nor hot, and the speaker says he will vomit it out. It boasts of being rich and self-sufficient, yet is wretched, poor, blind, and naked. It is counseled to buy gold, garments, and eye salve, and to repent zealously.

New Jerusalem is a holy city seen coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride and identified as the Lamb's wife. It is square, walled with twelve gates, and made of pure gold like clear glass, including its street. It has no temple, sun, or moon, because God and the Lamb are its temple and light. Its gates are never shut, yet only those written in the Lamb's book of life enter; the wicked are excluded.

determines fate in the lake of fire [anyone not written in it is cast into the lake] The book of life is opened, separately from the other books, at the judgment before the great white throne. Anyone not found written in it is cast into the lake of fire.

results_in being vomited out of the speaker's mouth Laodicea's works are neither cold nor hot, and the speaker says he wishes it were one or the other, because its lukewarmness leads him to vomit it out. It says it is rich and needs nothing, but does not know it is wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked. The speaker counsels it to buy gold, white garments, and eye salve and to repent.

God is the Lord God, the Almighty, who sits on the throne, appearing like jasper and sardius, and lives forever. He is worthy of glory, honor, and power because he created all things by his desire. He then holds a sealed seven-sealed book in his right hand, which the Lamb takes, and all creation praises him with the Lamb.

The throne is set in heaven with one sitting on it, surrounded by a rainbow like an emerald. Lightnings, sounds, and thunders proceed from it, and seven lamps of fire, the seven Spirits of God, burn before it. Before it is a sea of glass like crystal, and the four living creatures are in the middle of it and around it. Twenty-four other thrones surround it, and the elders throw their crowns before it.

The twenty-four elders are a group seated on twenty-four thrones around God's throne, wearing white garments and gold crowns. Their defining role is worship: they repeatedly fall down before God and throw their crowns before the throne. In Chapter 4 they declare God worthy of glory, honor, and power as creator. In Chapter 5 one elder comforts the narrator about the Lion of Judah, and after the Lamb takes the book they sing a new song, holding harps and golden bowls of incense, the prayers of the saints. In Chapter 11 they worship again, thanking God for reigning and speaking of judgment and reward.

The four living creatures stand in the middle of and around the throne, covered with eyes before, behind, around, and within, each with six wings. They resemble a lion, a calf, a man, and a flying eagle. In chapter 4 they ceaselessly praise God day and night, saying "Holy, holy, holy." In chapter 5 they fall before the Lamb with the elders, hold harps and golden incense bowls, sing the new song, and say "Amen."

Heaven has a door that is opened, through which a voice calls the narrator to come up. It contains the throne with the one sitting on it, the twenty-four thrones and elders, the seven lamps of fire, the sea of glass, and the four living creatures.

The four living creatures ceaselessly proclaim God's holiness and give him glory, honor, and thanks. In response, the twenty-four elders fall down before him, worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne. They declare him worthy to receive glory, honor, and power as creator of all things.

l: book (held by him who sat on the throne), Revelation
s: A book written inside and outside, sealed with seven seals, held in the right hand of him who sat on the throne. No one in heaven, on earth, or under the earth could open or look in it, until the Lamb took it from his hand.

The seven seals keep the book sealed shut. A mighty angel asks who is worthy to break them, and no one is found able until the one described as the Lion, who has overcome, is said to open the book and its seven seals. The Lamb is then praised as worthy to open them. Six of the seven seals are opened by the Lamb in this chapter. The first four release horses and riders, the fifth reveals the souls of the slain under the altar, and the sixth brings an earthquake and cosmic signs.

The Lamb is a central figure who appears standing in the middle of the throne, among the four living creatures and elders, looking as though slain, with seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent into all the earth. He is also called the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, and Lord of lords and King of kings. He is declared worthy to take the book and open its seals because he was killed and bought people for God with his blood, out of every tribe, language, people, and nation. He receives power, wealth, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, blessing, and worship from the elders, creatures, angels, and all created things. He then opens the first six of the seven seals, and his wrath, with that of the one on the throne, is what earth's people try to hide from. The great multitude praises him alongside God, having washed their robes in his blood, and he shepherds them to springs of life-giving waters. He stands on Mount Zion with the 144,000, who bear his and his Father's names. The ten kings war against him but he overcomes them, and his wedding to his ready wife is announced, with a blessing on those invited to the supper.

l: redeemed people (bought by the Lamb), Revelation
s: People bought for God by the Lamb's blood from every tribe, language, people and nation; made kings and priests to God, they will reign on earth.

A vast multitude of angels, numbering ten thousands of ten thousands and thousands of thousands, stands around the throne with the living creatures and elders. In Chapter 5, after a mighty angel asks who can open the book, they proclaim with loud voice that the slain Lamb is worthy.

Every created thing in heaven, on the earth, under the earth, and on the sea, and everything in them, is heard speaking. They offer blessing, honor, glory, and dominion forever to him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb.

The earth receives the fire thrown from the censer, followed by thunders, sounds, lightnings, and an earthquake. At the first trumpet, one third of the earth is burned up, along with one third of the trees and all green grass. The eagle announces woe to those who dwell on it.

The sea is a place struck by judgment: after the second trumpet a burning mountain turns one third to blood, killing a third of its creatures and ships; after the second bowl it becomes entirely blood.

Worship of the Lamb begins when the living creatures and elders fall down before him with harps and bowls of incense and sing a new song. It widens to include many angels and then every created thing, who join in ascribing blessing, honor, glory, and dominion to the one on the throne and the Lamb. It closes with the creatures' "Amen" and the elders falling down and worshiping.

l: rider on the white horse, Revelation
s: A rider on a white horse, armed with a bow, is given a crown and goes out conquering and to conquer.

l: rider on the red horse, Revelation
s: A rider on a red horse who, in Chapter 6, is given power to take peace from the earth, making people kill one another, and a great sword.

l: rider on the black horse, Revelation
s: A rider on a black horse holds a balance; in Chapter 6 a voice among the four living creatures announces grain prices (wheat, barley) and commands not to damage oil and wine.

Souls of those slain for the Word of God and the testimony of the Lamb, seen underneath the altar. They cry out for judgment and vengeance of their blood, receive white robes, and are told to rest a while until fellow servants complete their course.

l: great earthquake and cosmic signs, Revelation
s: At the sixth seal in Chapter 6, a great earthquake strikes: the sun turns black as sackcloth, the moon becomes blood, stars fall, the sky rolls up like a scroll, and mountains and islands move.

l: kings and people of the earth, Revelation
s: The kings and people of the earth are a broad collective spanning kings, princes, commanding officers, the rich, the strong, slaves and free. First, fleeing wrath, they hide in mountain caves and rocks, begging them to fall on them and conceal them from the one on the throne and the Lamb. Later, the earth's inhabitants marvel at the first beast, worship the dragon and beast, and are deceived by the second beast into making an image and bearing its mark, except those written in the Lamb's book of life.

l: great day of his wrath, Revelation
s: has_status has come The people of the earth declare that the great day of his wrath has come. They ask who is able to stand.

Four angels stand at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds so none blows on earth, sea, or trees. They were given the task of harming earth and sea, but are told to hold off until God's bondservants are sealed.
An angel rises from the sunrise bearing the seal of the living God and loudly commands four angels to withhold harm from earth, sea, and trees until God's bondservants are sealed on their foreheads.

The group is a body of 144,000 bondservants of God, sealed on their foreheads and drawn from every tribe of the children of Israel, 12,000 from each of twelve tribes. Later they stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion bearing his and his Father's name. Redeemed from the earth by Jesus, they alone can learn the new song, follow the Lamb wherever he goes, and are virgins, first fruits, blameless, with no lie in their mouth.

The great multitude is an uncountable crowd drawn from every nation, tribe, people and language. They stand before the throne and the Lamb in white robes holding palm branches, proclaiming salvation. They came out of great suffering and washed their robes in the Lamb's blood. They now serve God day and night in his temple, sheltered by him and shepherded by the Lamb to life-giving waters.

One of the elders, addressed as 'My lord' by the narrator, asks who the white-robed people are; when the narrator defers, he explains they came out of great suffering, washed in the Lamb's blood, and serve God.
Seven angels stand before God and receive seven trumpets; four sound, each bringing calamity, while three remain still to sound.

held_by seven angels Seven trumpets are given to the seven angels who stand before God. Four are sounded in this unit, each followed by a destructive event affecting a third of the earth, sea, waters, or heavenly lights, and three are still to come.

l: angel with the golden censer, Revelation
s: An angel holding a golden censer stands over the altar, is given much incense to add to the saints' prayers, sends smoke up before God, then fills the censer with altar fire and throws it to earth, causing thunders, lightnings, and an earthquake.

The first trumpet blast, in Chapter 8, occurs when the first angel sounds: hail and fire mixed with blood are thrown to the earth, burning up one third of the earth, one third of the trees, and all green grass.
Wormwood is a great star that falls burning like a torch from the sky at the third trumpet, striking a third of rivers and springs, turning a third of the waters bitter, and causing many deaths.
An eagle flying in mid heaven after the fourth trumpet cries aloud a threefold woe to earth's inhabitants, warning of the three trumpet blasts still to come.
The fifth angel sounds his trumpet, which begins the first woe. After he sounds, a star fallen from the sky is seen receiving the key to the abyss.

l: star (fallen from the sky, fifth angel), Revelation
s: A star fallen from the sky to the earth after the fifth angel sounds; it is given the key to the abyss's pit and opens it.

emits smoke from the pit [when opened] The pit is opened with the key given to the fallen star, and smoke like that of a burning furnace rises from it, darkening the sun and the air. Locusts come out of the smoke, and the pit's king is the angel of the abyss.

Locusts emerge from smoke on the earth with scorpion-like power, forbidden to harm vegetation and permitted only to torment, not kill, people lacking God's seal for five months. They resemble war horses with golden crowns, human faces, women's hair, lions' teeth, iron breastplates, noisy wings and stinging scorpion tails, ruled by Abaddon, the angel of the abyss.

lacks God [seal on foreheads] People who lack God's seal on their foreheads are the only ones the locusts are allowed to hurt. They are tormented for five months as by a scorpion's sting, so that they seek death but cannot find it, and death flees from them.
Abaddon, Hebrew name of the angel of the abyss and king over the locusts, is also called Apollyon in Greek.

has_possession trumpet The sixth angel sounds his trumpet after the first woe has passed. A voice from the horns of the golden altar before God tells him to free the four angels bound at the Euphrates.

Four angels bound at the great river Euphrates, prepared for a specific hour, day, month, and year, are held until the sixth angel orders their release, whereupon they are to kill one third of mankind.

has_disposition unrepentant [the rest who survived the plagues] One third of mankind is killed by the fire, smoke, and sulfur from the horses' mouths. The rest, who survive these plagues, do not repent of worshiping demons and idols, nor of their murders, sorceries, sexual immorality, or thefts.

An army of horsemen numbering two hundred million, heard by the narrator; riders wear fiery red, hyacinth blue and sulfur yellow breastplates, horses have lions' heads, and fire, smoke, sulfur from their mouths and serpent-like tails harm.
kills mankind [one third] The three plagues are the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur that proceed out of the horses' mouths. By them one third of mankind is killed.

The mighty angel is a figure seen in a vision, descending from the sky clothed with a cloud, with a rainbow on his head, a sun-like face, and fiery pillar-like feet. He stands with his right foot on the sea and left on the land, holding a little open book. He cries like a roaring lion, then raises his hand and swears by the eternal Creator that delay is over and God's mystery will be finished when the seventh angel sounds. He finally gives the book to the narrator to eat, bitter in the stomach, sweet in the mouth.

l: little book (in the angel's hand), Revelation
s: The little book is held open in the mighty angel's hand as he stands on the sea and the land. The narrator is told to take it, and he does and eats it. It is as sweet as honey in his mouth, but it makes his stomach bitter.

has_utterances sealed [narrator told not to write them] The seven thunders utter their voices when the angel cries out with a loud voice like a lion's roar. The narrator is about to write what they said, but a voice from the sky commands him to seal up their words and not write them, so their content remains undisclosed.
The mystery of God, declared by God to his servants the prophets, is sworn by an angel in Chapter 10 to be finished in the days of the seventh angel's voice, as he is about to sound.

The two witnesses are two olive trees and two lamp stands standing before the Lord of the earth. Empowered by God, they prophesy 1,260 days in sackcloth, torment earth's inhabitants, and wield fire from their mouths, sky-shutting, water-to-blood, and plagues. After finishing their testimony, the beast from the abyss kills them. After three and a half days God's breath enters them, they stand, and enemies watch as they ascend to heaven in a cloud.

l: temple of the tabernacle of the testimony, Revelation
s: The heavenly temple of the tabernacle of the testimony is God's temple. In Chapter 11 the narrator measures it, its altar and worshippers, while the outer court is left to the nations. In Chapter 15 it opens, seven angels emerge, and smoke from God's glory fills it, barring entry until the seven plagues finish.

The holy city is first trodden underfoot by the nations for forty-two months. It is then shown containing the river of life and the throne of God and the Lamb, with no curse or night. Commandment-keepers enter its gates, wrongdoers stay outside, and anyone removing the book's words loses his part.

Babylon the great is a symbolic great and strong city, portrayed also as a woman, whose name is written on her forehead. She is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt and is the place where the Lord was crucified. She reigns over the kings of the earth, sits on the waters, on a beast, and on seven mountains, dressed in purple and scarlet, adorned with gold, precious stones and pearls, and holding a golden cup full of abominations. Most important is her guilt: she made the nations drink the wine of her sexual immorality, deceived them with sorcery, enriched merchants through her luxury, and is drunk with the blood of saints, martyrs, prophets and all the slain. She glorifies herself and says in her heart she sits a queen and will see no mourning. The records unfold from the great city in which the witnesses' bodies lie and an earthquake topples a tenth of it, to an angel's declaration that she has fallen. At the seventh bowl she is remembered before God and given the cup of his wrath. She becomes a habitation of demons and a prison of unclean spirits, is repaid double, burned and made desolate in one hour. God judges her and avenges his servants, and her smoke goes up forever and ever.
comes_from abyss The beast that comes up out of the abyss makes war on the two witnesses once they finish their testimony. It overcomes and kills them.

The abyss is the place into which the dragon is cast, shut, and sealed so that he cannot deceive the nations for a thousand years. Its key is held by the descending angel. Satan is released from this prison after the thousand years.

l: those who dwell on the earth, Revelation
s: disposition_toward_witnesses rejoice over their deaths [give gifts to one another] Those who dwell on the earth rejoice and are glad over the dead witnesses, giving gifts to one another because the two prophets had tormented them. People from the peoples, tribes, languages, and nations look at the bodies for three and a half days and refuse to let them be buried.

causes_death_of seven thousand people [a tenth of the city fell] A great earthquake occurs on the day the witnesses ascend, causing a tenth of the city to fall and killing seven thousand people. The rest are terrified and give glory to the God of heaven.
God's heavenly temple, containing the ark of the Lord's covenant, is opened and the ark seen, followed by lightnings, thunders, earthquake, and hail.

becomes Kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ [he will reign forever and ever] After the seventh angel sounds, loud voices in heaven declare that the kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of the Lord and of his Christ. He will reign forever and ever.

l: woman clothed with the sun, Revelation
s: A woman appearing as a great heavenly sign, clothed with the sun, the moon under her feet, and a crown of twelve stars. She cries out in labor and bears a son. She then flees to a place God prepared in the wilderness, nourished 1,260 days, aided by eagle wings and the earth, and has further offspring.
The woman's son, a male child destined to rule all nations with a rod of iron, is born, escapes the dragon who wanted to devour him, and is caught up to God's throne.
Michael leads angels against the dragon in the heavenly war; he and his angels prevail, and the dragon's forces are cast out of heaven.
The brothers are accused before God day and night by the accuser, yet they overcame him through the Lamb's blood and their testimony, not loving their lives even to death.

l: rest of the woman's offspring, Revelation
s: The woman's remaining offspring, who keep God's commandments and hold Jesus' testimony; the angry dragon leaves to make war on them.

has_no_place_for dragon [and his angels] Heaven is the setting of the signs of the woman and the dragon and of the war in which the dragon and his angels lose their place. A loud voice there proclaims God's salvation and Kingdom, and the heavens and their inhabitants are told to rejoice because the accuser has been thrown down.

helps woman clothed with the sun [swallowed the river] The dragon draws a third of the stars to the earth, and later he and his angels are thrown down onto it. The earth and the sea are warned of woe because the devil has come down in great wrath. The earth helps the woman by opening its mouth and swallowing the river the dragon spewed.

has_outcome dragon and his angels did not prevail Michael and his angels fight the dragon and his angels in the sky. The dragon's side does not prevail and no place is found for them in heaven, so the dragon, the old serpent, and his angels are thrown down to the earth.

The beast is a composite, blasphemous ruler who rises out of the sea with ten horns crowned with ten crowns, seven heads bearing blasphemous names, and a leopard-like body with bear's feet and a lion's mouth. The dragon gives it power, throne, and great authority, and one of its heads has a fatal wound that is healed. For forty-two months it blasphemes God, makes war on the saints and overcomes them, and holds authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation. Those who dwell on the earth, whose names are not in the book of life, worship it, and its mark is received on forehead or hand; worshippers are warned of torment and God's wrath. Later its throne is struck by the fifth bowl and its kingdom is darkened, while a frog-like spirit comes from its mouth to gather kings for war. It appears scarlet and full of blasphemous names, carrying the woman. Its heads and horns represent seven and ten kings; it is described as an eighth who is of the seven, destined to come up from the abyss and go to destruction. The ten kings give it their power and kingdom, and it joins them in burning the prostitute. Finally, gathered with the kings and armies against the rider on the horse, it is taken and thrown alive into the lake of fire.

The second beast rises out of the earth with two lamb-like horns yet speaks like a dragon. It wields the first beast's full authority in his presence and compels the earth's inhabitants to worship him. Through great signs, including fire from the sky, it deceives them into making an image, gives that image breath to speak, and imposes the mark on all people.

The image of the beast is an object made for the first beast, the one with the sword wound who lived. Made at the second beast's urging, it is given breath and speaks, causing those who refuse to worship it to be killed.
The mark of the beast is the name of the beast or the number of his name, placed on the right hands or foreheads of all people by the second beast, and required to buy or sell.

is_number_of the first beast [the number of a man] The number 666 is given as the number of the beast and is said to be the number of a man. The text calls for wisdom and understanding from anyone who would calculate it.

l: saints and martyrs of Jesus, Revelation
s: The saints and martyrs of Jesus are a group warred upon and overcome by the first beast; facing captivity and death by the sword, their defining mark is endurance and faith.

has_message Good News [eternal, to every nation, tribe, language, and people] The first angel flies in mid heaven with an eternal Good News for every nation, tribe, language and people. He cries with a loud voice to fear and glorify God and worship the Creator, because the hour of his judgment has come.

l: people with the mark of the beast, Revelation
s: This group consists of people who receive the mark of the beast on forehead or hand and worship the beast's image. Chapter 14 describes their fate: drinking God's unmixed wrath, being tormented with fire and sulfur before the holy angels and the Lamb, with smoke rising forever and no rest. Chapter 16 shows them afflicted with painful sores from the first bowl, scorched, blaspheming God, and refusing to repent.

l: great wine press of the wrath of God, Revelation
s: The great wine press of the wrath of God receives the earth's vintage from an angel, is trodden outside the city, and yields blood rising to horses' bridles across 1,600 stadia.

has_state ripe An angel from the temple announces that the hour to reap has come and the harvest of the earth is ripe. The earth is reaped by the one on the cloud, and then the earth's grape clusters, fully ripe, are gathered by another angel with a sharp sickle and thrown into the wine press.

has_state come [the hour has arrived] The first angel proclaims that the hour of God's judgment has come. It is shown in Babylon's fall, in the torment of the beast's worshippers, and in the reaping of the earth and the treading of the wine press of God's wrath.

Seven angels carry the seven last plagues. Dressed in pure, bright linen with golden sashes, they emerge from the opened heavenly temple, and one of the four living creatures gives them golden bowls full of God's wrath. Commanded by a loud voice from the temple, each pours out his bowl in turn on the earth, sea, rivers and springs, sun, the beast's throne, the Euphrates, and the air.
completes wrath of God [final plagues] The seven last plagues are held by the seven angels, and in them God's wrath is finished. No one can enter the temple until these plagues are completed.
God's wrath is said to be finished in the seven last plagues. It is contained in seven golden bowls given to the seven angels.

l: overcomers (those who overcame the beast), Revelation
s: Overcomers of the beast, its image, and its name's number stand on a sea of glass mixed with fire, holding God's harps and singing the song of Moses and the Lamb; they receive the water of life freely.

l: song of Moses and the Lamb, Revelation
s: The overcomers sing this song, which declares God's works great and marvelous and his ways righteous and true. It asks who would not fear and glorify him, proclaims him alone holy, and says all nations will come and worship because his righteous acts have been revealed.
contains wrath of God Seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God are given to the seven angels by one of the four living creatures.

l: seven bowls of the wrath of God, Revelation
s: is_a wrath of God The bowls are poured out one after another, bringing sores, blood in the sea and waters, scorching heat, darkness on the beast's kingdom, the drying of the Euphrates, and finally a great earthquake and hail. They are the means of God's judgment on the earth.

The false prophet works signs in the beast's sight to deceive those bearing the beast's mark and worshiping his image; he is finally captured with the beast and thrown alive into the burning lake of fire.

is_a place [called so in Hebrew; where the kings are gathered] Harmagedon is the place, called so in Hebrew, where the kings of the whole inhabited earth are gathered together. They are gathered for the war of the great day of God the Almighty.

has_attribute unprecedented in magnitude [greatest since men were on earth] The great earthquake follows the seventh bowl, with lightnings, sounds, and thunders. It is described as greater than any since men have been on the earth, dividing the great city into three parts, felling the cities of the nations, and causing every island to flee and the mountains to vanish.
has_weight about a talent Great hailstones, each about the weight of a talent, fall from the sky on people. The plague is called exceedingly severe, and people blaspheme God because of it.

l: angel (one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls), Revelation
s: One of the seven angels holding the seven bowls; in Chapter 17 he calls the narrator, shows the great prostitute's judgment, and explains the mystery of the woman, beast, heads, horns, and waters, identifying her as the great city.

Ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom but receive authority with the beast for one hour. Unified in one mind, they give their power to the beast and war against the Lamb. Together with the beast they hate the prostitute, desolating, stripping, devouring and burning her, fulfilling God's purpose placed in their hearts.

has_relationship_with Babylon the great [committed sexual immorality and lived wantonly with her] The kings of the earth committed sexual immorality and lived wantonly with Babylon. They will weep and wail when they see the smoke of her burning, standing far away in fear of her torment and lamenting that her judgment came in one hour.

l: judgment of the great prostitute, Revelation
s: is_shown_to John (narrator) [by the angel] The angel offers to show this judgment to the narrator, who sees the prostitute sitting on many waters, which are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages. The judgment is carried out when the ten horns and the beast hate her, make her desolate, strip her, eat her flesh, and burn her utterly with fire, until God's words are accomplished.

l: angel (coming down out of the sky), Revelation
s: An angel of great authority descends from the sky, lighting the earth with his glory, and cries mightily that Babylon the great has fallen, a haunt of demons, because nations, kings, and merchants shared her immorality.

is_a angel [mighty] The mighty angel takes up a stone like a great millstone and casts it into the sea. He declares that Babylon will be thrown down with violence and found no more, and that music, craftsmen, the mill, lamplight, and the voices of bridegroom and bride will cease in her.

belongs_to God [called 'my people' by a voice from heaven] A voice from heaven calls them to come out of Babylon so that they have no participation in her sins and do not receive her plagues. They are also told to repay her double according to her works.

The merchants of the earth, styled princes of the earth, grew rich from Babylon the great's luxury. When she falls, no one buys their goods, and they stand far off weeping, lamenting that such riches were desolated in an hour.

Ship masters, sailors, and mariners who earned their living by sea were enriched by Babylon the great. As she burns, they stand far off, throw dust on their heads, weep, and mourn her wealth's desolation in one hour.

Babylon's destruction is a sudden, fiery downfall in one day and one hour, shown by a millstone cast into the sea. It brings death, famine, and silence; heaven and the saints rejoice while kings, merchants, and sailors mourn.

l: Faithful and True (rider on the white horse), Revelation
s: Faithful and True is a figure who appears when heaven opens, riding a white horse and judging and making war in righteousness. He has eyes like fire, many crowns, a blood-sprinkled garment, the name The Word of God, and the title KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS on his garment and thigh. A sharp sword comes from his mouth. He treads God's wine press of wrath, defeats the beast and false prophet, kills the rest with his sword, and rules the nations with an iron rod.

praises God [declares his judgments true and righteous] The great multitude cries Hallelujah, praising God for salvation, power, and glory and for his true and righteous judgments on the great prostitute. Their voice is like many waters and mighty thunders as they declare that the Lord God Almighty reigns and call for rejoicing because the wedding of the Lamb has come.

l: bride (New Jerusalem as a bride), Revelation
s: The Lamb's wife, a collective bride, readies herself for the wedding, given bright, pure linen representing the saints' righteous acts, and joins the Spirit in saying Come.

l: angel (who showed John these things), Revelation
s: An angel sent by Jesus to testify to the assemblies. He shows John the river and tree of life, affirms the words are faithful and true, then refuses John's worship, identifying himself as a fellow bondservant and directing worship to God.
Heavenly armies, dressed in white, pure, fine linen, follow the rider Faithful and True on white horses in Chapter 19; they do not fight, as his sword kills the rest.

l: kings of the earth and their armies, Revelation
s: opposes Faithful and True (rider on the white horse) [gathered to make war] The kings of the earth and their armies gather with the beast to make war against him who sat on the horse and his army. They are killed with the sword that comes out of the rider's mouth, and the birds are filled with their flesh.

l: angel (who came down out of heaven), Revelation
s: An angel descends from heaven holding the abyss key and a great chain, seizes the dragon (the old serpent, devil, Satan), binds him a thousand years, and casts him into the sealed abyss.
The thousand years is a period when Satan is bound in the abyss and the faithful reign with Christ while the rest of the dead stay lifeless; it ends with Satan's release and the final war.

l: martyrs and faithful saints who reign with Christ, Revelation
s: A group of martyrs and faithful saints, beheaded for testifying to Jesus and refusing to worship the beast, its image, or its mark. They are given thrones and judgment, live and reign with Christ a thousand years, blessed, holy, priests of God and Christ, immune to the second death.

is_a resurrection of those who reign with Christ [those who have part in it are blessed and holy] The first resurrection is when the martyrs and faithful come to life and reign with Christ, while the rest of the dead stay dead until the thousand years finish. Those who share in it are called blessed and holy, and the second death has no power over them.
Gog and Magog are nations from the earth's four corners, deceived by Satan after his release, gathered for war in countless numbers like sea sand, then devoured by fire from heaven.

l: the final war against the saints, Revelation
s: The final war against the saints: after Satan's release, deceived nations spread across the earth and surround the saints' camp and the beloved city, until fire from heaven devours them and the devil is thrown into the lake of fire.

is_occupied_by God [the one from whose face earth and sky fled] The great white throne is the seat of the one before whose face the earth and sky flee away, leaving no place for them. The dead, great and small, stand before it to be judged.

The final judgment is an event in which the dead, given up by the sea, Death, and Hades, stand before the great white throne and are judged by their works from opened books; Death, Hades, and those not in the book of life are cast into the lake of fire.

is_given_up_by the sea [also by Death and Hades] The rest of the dead do not live until the thousand years are finished. Later the dead, great and small, are given up by the sea, Death, and Hades, and stand before the throne to be judged by their works as written in the books.

l: new heaven and new earth, Revelation
s: The new heaven and new earth, seen by the narrator, replaces the first heaven and earth, which pass away. It has no sea, and no death, mourning, crying or pain, as God makes all things new.

l: angel (one of the seven angels with the bowls), Revelation
s: One of the seven angels holding the bowls of the last plagues. He invites the narrator to see the Lamb's bride, carries him to a high mountain, shows him the holy city, and measures its gates and walls with a golden reed, by an angel's measure.

This prophecy book is declared faithful and true, left unsealed because the time is at hand. It blesses those who keep its words and guards itself: adding to it brings its written plagues, while removing from it forfeits one's part in the tree of life and holy city.

has_timing soon Jesus announces three times in this chapter that he is coming soon, in verses 7, 12, and 20. His coming brings a reward that repays each person according to his work, and blessing for those who keep the words of the prophecy. The book ends with the response "Yes, come, Lord Jesus!"
